what: Lincoln Electric makes welding equipment: the machines, the wire and electrodes they consume, and the robotic cells that weld in factories. The consumables are bought again and again.
customers: Shipyards, pipeline builders, heavy equipment makers, car plants and the welding schools that train on its machines.
money: machines and consumables in North and South America
the same products in Europe and Asia
moat: Welders train on Lincoln machines and buy Lincoln wire for them, and a welding procedure qualified with one consumable is not casually changed. The razor-and-blade pattern is unusually durable here.
risks: Revenue has been flat around $4.2B for three years, tied to industrial capital spending
Steel and copper prices move the cost of consumables faster than prices can be reset
Automation projects are discretionary and are the first thing customers postpone
opportunities: A 12.3% net margin and $512M of free cash flow, high for a machinery maker
Analysts see about 21% upside, and the company has raised its dividend for about thirty years
Reshoring of American manufacturing means new plants, and new plants need welding
watch: Organic sales growth and orders for automation systems.
